1a7160e43377ec611bbccec3f2760f179948fd79.overview: This trial is for Black and Latino adults in Harlem who screen at moderate risk for depression on the PHQ-4. It tests whether a community coalition, led by a health insurer working with community organizations and medical, behavioral health, and social service providers, improves mental health care. The care is delivered through task-sharing, where community health workers screen, educate, and refer. The study uses a hybrid implementation-effectiveness design.

inclusion.criterion: Black or Latino adults aged 18 to 65 years
inclusion.plain: Check that the patient identifies as Black or Latino and is aged 18-65

inclusion.criterion: Harlem resident in low-income housing developments or receiving primary care services in Harlem
inclusion.plain: Check that the patient lives in Harlem low-income housing or gets primary care in Harlem

inclusion.criterion: PHQ-4 Total Score ≥3, moderate risk for depression
inclusion.plain: Check for a current PHQ-4 total of ≥3

exclusion.criterion: Screens positive for severe mental illness (e.g., psychosis, mania, substance abuse, high suicide risk) on MINI screening items
exclusion.plain: Check the MINI screen for psychosis, mania, substance abuse, or high suicide risk; if positive, exclude and refer to a higher level of MH care

screening_notes: The PHQ-4 must be given to confirm a total score of ≥3.
The Mini-International Neuropsychiatric Interview (MINI) screening items must be given to rule out psychosis, mania, substance abuse, and high suicide risk.
Patients who screen positive on the MINI are excluded and referred to MH services at higher levels of care.
Confirm self-identified race/ethnicity (Black or Latino) and whether the patient lives in Harlem low-income housing or gets primary care in Harlem.
1a7160e43377ec611bbccec3f2760f179948fd79.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
1a7160e43377ec611bbccec3f2760f179948fd79.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
1a7160e43377ec611bbccec3f2760f179948fd79.involves: Stepped-wedge cluster-randomized study where sites move in sequence through 3 conditions: online education and resources on task-sharing (E&R), then a community-engaged multisector collaborative care model (MCC), then MCC plus a crowdsourced technology tool (MCC+Tech). No placebo; visit schedule and duration not stated.

4ecaf6aa18967163cb8fe91751af1b7d27d3368e.overview: The trial is looking for adults aged 18 to 25 whose primary diagnosis is an anxiety, depressive, or bipolar disorder. It randomizes them to one of two versions of the Maya mobile CBT app. In the standard version, new skills can be introduced across all 6 weeks. In the personalized version, skills are matched to the participant's symptoms and all new material comes in the first 4 weeks. The investigators expect the shorter, less demanding personalized version to work as well for anxiety and depression symptoms.

inclusion.criterion: Age between 18 and 25 years (any sex)
inclusion.plain: Confirm date of birth: age 18–25

inclusion.criterion: Primary anxiety, depressive, or bipolar disorder, with a score of 4 or greater on the ADIS Clinical Severity Rating
inclusion.plain: Primary diagnosis must be anxiety, depressive, or bipolar, with ADIS Clinical Severity Rating ≥4

inclusion.criterion: If bipolar, currently euthymic or in a depressive episode
inclusion.plain: For bipolar patients, confirm current mood state is euthymic or depressed

inclusion.criterion: Access to an Apple iPhone, iPad, or Android device
inclusion.plain: Ask whether the patient has a compatible smartphone or tablet

exclusion.criterion: History of neurologic disorder that may affect the neural systems of interest or ability to participate
exclusion.plain: Check the chart for a neurologic history (e.g., seizures, TBI)

exclusion.criterion: Lifetime diagnosis of a psychotic disorder
exclusion.plain: Check for any past or current psychotic disorder diagnosis

exclusion.criterion: Current hypomanic or manic episode
exclusion.plain: Rule out current hypomania or mania

exclusion.criterion: Currently in cognitive behavior therapy
exclusion.plain: Confirm the patient is not in CBT right now

exclusion.criterion: Change in dose of a psychiatric medication in the past 12 weeks
exclusion.plain: Check that psychiatric medication doses have not changed for 12 weeks

exclusion.criterion: Initiation of psychotherapy in the past 12 weeks
exclusion.plain: Check that no psychotherapy was started in the past 12 weeks

exclusion.criterion: Intent or plan to attempt suicide
exclusion.plain: Assess current suicidal intent or plan

screening_notes: ADIS interview by the study team is needed to confirm the primary diagnosis and a Clinical Severity Rating ≥4
Bipolar patients need a current mood-state assessment: must be euthymic or depressed, with no current hypomania or mania
Suicide risk screen needed to rule out intent or plan
Review medication history for dose changes and therapy history for any psychotherapy started in the past 12 weeks or current CBT
Neurologic history must be reviewed; the trial excludes disorders that may affect the neural systems of interest (relevant to the optional EEG)
4ecaf6aa18967163cb8fe91751af1b7d27d3368e.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
4ecaf6aa18967163cb8fe91751af1b7d27d3368e.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
4ecaf6aa18967163cb8fe91751af1b7d27d3368e.involves: Randomized to standard or personalized Maya mobile CBT app (no placebo arm described). App use 2 days/week, ≥20 min/day, for 6 weeks, plus weekly research check-ins. Assessments at baseline, week 4, week 6, and week 12 follow-up. Optional EEG at baseline and week 6.

78f37ce42e2699009edd6d1141f43a32ccaac6aa.overview: This is the team's reference protocol for adults aged 18–65 with moderate generalized anxiety disorder (GAD-7 10 to 14) and depressive symptoms below the moderately severe range (PHQ-9 below 15). The study wants participants who have not taken antidepressants or sedatives recently and who do not have major psychiatric comorbidities.

inclusion.criterion: Age 18 to 65 inclusive (registry: 18 Years to 65 Years, sex: ALL)
inclusion.plain: Confirm DOB: age 18–65 inclusive; any sex

inclusion.criterion: GAD-7 score 10 to 14 (moderate range)
inclusion.plain: Current GAD-7 between 10 and 14

inclusion.criterion: PHQ-9 score below 15
inclusion.plain: Current PHQ-9 under 15

inclusion.criterion: Symptom duration at least 3 months
inclusion.plain: Charted anxiety symptoms for at least 3 months

inclusion.criterion: Able to attend in-person or telehealth visits
inclusion.plain: Patient can attend visits in person or by telehealth

inclusion.criterion: Provides informed consent as an adult
inclusion.plain: Has capacity to consent; no guardian/proxy consent

exclusion.criterion: Current SSRI or SNRI, or any antidepressant within 4 weeks (washout)
exclusion.plain: Med list: no SSRI/SNRI now and no antidepressant in past 4 weeks

exclusion.criterion: Benzodiazepine or sedative-hypnotic use, including OTC sleep aids
exclusion.plain: No benzodiazepines, Z-drugs, or OTC sleep aids

exclusion.criterion: Current suicidality, or suicidal behavior within 12 months
exclusion.plain: No current suicidality and no suicidal behavior in past 12 months

exclusion.criterion: Active substance use disorder within 6 months
exclusion.plain: No active SUD in past 6 months

exclusion.criterion: Bereavement within 6 months
exclusion.plain: No death of a loved one in past 6 months

exclusion.criterion: Enrollment in another GAD trial within 12 months
exclusion.plain: No other GAD trial in past 12 months

exclusion.criterion: Bipolar, psychotic, or primary panic disorder (requires screening)
exclusion.plain: No bipolar, psychotic, or primary panic disorder diagnosis; screening required

screening_notes: I-2/I-3: Give the GAD-7 (10 to 14) and PHQ-9 (below 15) now; older scores may not be valid
I-6: Confirm the patient can consent as an adult
E-1/E-2: Review all medications, including OTC sleep aids. Patients who took any antidepressant in the past 4 weeks are excluded
E-3: A suicide risk interview is needed to cover current suicidality and behavior in the past 12 months
E-4: Screen for substance use disorder in the past 6 months
E-5: Ask about bereavement in the past 6 months; this is often not in the chart
E-6: Ask about any GAD trial in the past 12 months
E-7: The protocol requires screening for bipolar, psychotic, and primary panic disorder (structured interview advised)
78f37ce42e2699009edd6d1141f43a32ccaac6aa.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
78f37ce42e2699009edd6d1141f43a32ccaac6aa.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
78f37ce42e2699009edd6d1141f43a32ccaac6aa.involves: Intervention, number of visits, length of the study, and placebo use are not stated in the record; visits can be in person or by telehealth.

671cf1f8ea27f0cbea29aff6278b1e22ceef01bb.overview: This study tests SilverCloud, a clinician-guided app-based CBT program, as a school-based mental health intervention for vulnerable youth aged 13 to 22 who screen positive for anxiety or depression symptoms. It runs in two phases. Phase I is an open trial. After the program is refined, an RCT will randomize students who seek or are referred for mental health services at a study site to SilverCloud or treatment as usual (TAU).

inclusion.criterion: Age 13 Years to 22 Years; all sexes
inclusion.plain: Confirm age is 13-22

inclusion.criterion: Phase I open trial: enrolled in a high school
inclusion.plain: Confirm current high school enrollment

inclusion.criterion: RCT: enrolled in 9th through 11th grades
inclusion.plain: Confirm grade is 9, 10, or 11

inclusion.criterion: RCT: enrolled in one of the study sites
inclusion.plain: Confirm the student attends a participating study site

inclusion.criterion: Both phases: score of 10+ on GAD-7 or PHQ-9
inclusion.plain: GAD-7 ≥10 or PHQ-9 ≥10

inclusion.criterion: Both phases: speaks/reads English (the SilverCloud version is English-only)
inclusion.plain: Confirm English speaking and reading ability

exclusion.criterion: Both phases: does not use a smartphone
exclusion.plain: Confirm the patient uses a smartphone

exclusion.criterion: Both phases: mental health concerns for which intensive treatment is indicated (e.g., mania or psychosis)
exclusion.plain: Rule out mania, psychosis, or any need for a higher level of care

exclusion.criterion: Both phases: current suicidal ideation with intent (plan and intent to act)
exclusion.plain: Check for an active suicide plan or intent; can re-screen once thoughts have abated

exclusion.criterion: RCT only: current (within 1 month of enrollment) mental health treatment at one of the study sites
exclusion.plain: Check for any treatment at a study site in the past 1 month

screening_notes: Give the GAD-7 and PHQ-9; eligibility needs a score of 10+ on either one.
Clinical interview to rule out mania or psychosis, or any need for intensive treatment.

Suicide risk assessment: anyone with a plan and intent goes to the SBHC suicide risk protocol (Phase I) or to crisis intervention through the referring site (RCT). They can be re-screened once their suicidal thoughts have abated.
The phases have different criteria: Phase I takes any high school student, while the RCT is limited to grades 9-11 at a study site with no study-site mental health treatment in the past 1 month.
Ask about smartphone use and English reading ability.
671cf1f8ea27f0cbea29aff6278b1e22ceef01bb.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
671cf1f8ea27f0cbea29aff6278b1e22ceef01bb.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
671cf1f8ea27f0cbea29aff6278b1e22ceef01bb.involves: Clinician-guided app-based CBT program (SilverCloud), with self-report outcome measures and feasibility/acceptability interviews. Phase I is an open trial; the RCT randomizes to SilverCloud or TAU, with no placebo. The record does not state visit schedule or duration.

3b89d3906d47eafce834582b229af4b6b2581840.overview: This randomized controlled trial is looking for adults aged 18 to 60 whose primary diagnosis is social anxiety disorder (SAD) and who score at least 50 on the LSAS self-report. It compares two forms of a brief computer-based therapy to see whether they are feasible, acceptable and effective, and how they work. It also uses MRI to measure the treatment's effect on brain activity.

inclusion.criterion: Males and females aged 18 to 60
inclusion.plain: Confirm age 18–60; any sex

inclusion.criterion: Current primary diagnosis of SAD
inclusion.plain: SAD is the current primary diagnosis

inclusion.criterion: Score of at least 50 on the Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale (self-rated version)
inclusion.plain: LSAS self-report score ≥50

inclusion.criterion: Fluent in English
inclusion.plain: Check English fluency

inclusion.criterion: Willing and able to give informed written consent
inclusion.plain: Has capacity and is willing to give written consent

inclusion.criterion: Ability to participate responsibly in the protocol
inclusion.plain: Can reliably attend and follow the protocol

inclusion.criterion: Normal or corrected-to-normal vision
inclusion.plain: Vision is adequate (with glasses/contacts if needed) for computer tasks

exclusion.criterion: Present or past psychotic episode, psychotic disorder, schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, or bipolar disorder
exclusion.plain: Any lifetime psychosis, schizophrenia-spectrum or bipolar disorder

exclusion.criterion: Current severe depression
exclusion.plain: Current severe depressive episode

exclusion.criterion: Suicidal ideation or behavior
exclusion.plain: Any suicidal ideation or behavior

exclusion.criterion: Current PTSD, OCD, bipolar disorder, manic episode, or tic disorder
exclusion.plain: Current PTSD, OCD, bipolar disorder, mania, or tic disorder

exclusion.criterion: Current or past organic mental disorder, seizure disorder, epilepsy, or brain injury
exclusion.plain: Lifetime organic mental disorder, seizures/epilepsy, or brain injury

exclusion.criterion: Current unstable or untreated medical illness
exclusion.plain: Any medical illness that is unstable or untreated

exclusion.criterion: Severe alcohol or cannabis use disorder; any severity of other substance use disorder (nicotine excepted)
exclusion.plain: Severe AUD/CUD, or any other SUD except nicotine

exclusion.criterion: Psychiatric medication in past month other than SSRIs, SNRIs, buspirone, or zolpidem for sleep at a stable dose for at least 3 months
exclusion.plain: Med list for past month: only SSRI/SNRI/buspirone/zolpidem (sleep) allowed, at a stable dose for ≥3 months

exclusion.criterion: Concurrent CBT or other psychotherapy initiated in the past 3 months
exclusion.plain: No psychotherapy started within the past 3 months

exclusion.criterion: Contraindication to MRI scanning
exclusion.plain: MRI safety screen (implants, metal, claustrophobia, etc.)

screening_notes: Diagnostic interview needed to confirm SAD is primary and to rule out current or lifetime exclusionary diagnoses (psychosis, bipolar, PTSD, OCD, tic disorder, severe depression, SUD severity)
LSAS self-report must be given; score ≥50 required
Suicide risk assessment for any ideation or behavior
Medication reconciliation: check past-month psychiatric meds and that dose has been stable for ≥3 months
Ask about psychotherapy start dates (none started in past 3 months)
MRI safety screening questionnaire
Review medical history for unstable/untreated illness, seizures, and brain injury
Judgment-based items: ability to participate responsibly; capacity to consent
3b89d3906d47eafce834582b229af4b6b2581840.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
3b89d3906d47eafce834582b229af4b6b2581840.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
3b89d3906d47eafce834582b229af4b6b2581840.involves: Randomized to one of two forms of computer-based therapy: 8 sessions of 30 minutes over 4 weeks, plus MRI scanning; no placebo arm is stated.

62a85b0d9788c8be2544cbc41aee6c1508010e2e.overview: This trial is looking for autistic youth aged 8-14 from high-need or underserved communities who also have clinically significant anxiety. It tests whether EEG brain-activity measures change along with anxiety symptoms after Facing Your Fears (FYF) CBT. Participants are compared with a waitlist group that continues treatment as usual.

inclusion.criterion: Age 8 to 14 years (any sex)
inclusion.plain: Confirm DOB: age 8-14.

inclusion.criterion: Significant deficits in reciprocal social behavior: parent-report SCQ score of 11 or above
inclusion.plain: Parent SCQ ≥11 (done at screening if not in the chart).

inclusion.criterion: Verbally fluent in English, enough for ADOS-2 Module 3 or 4 (given by the researchers)
inclusion.plain: Check fluent English speech; researchers confirm Module 3/4 fit.

inclusion.criterion: Estimated verbal IQ of 70 or above on KBIT-2 (given by the researchers)
inclusion.plain: No known verbal IQ below 70; researchers test with KBIT-2.

inclusion.criterion: Clinically significant anxiety: significant elevations on parent-report SCARED or PRAS-ASD
inclusion.plain: Check for anxiety; parent SCARED or PRAS-ASD must be significantly elevated.

inclusion.criterion: Legal guardian gives consent and takes part in FYF with the child, or approves another caregiver who lives with the child (named on the consent form)
inclusion.plain: Guardian can consent, and a guardian or live-in caregiver can attend FYF sessions.

exclusion.criterion: Fails to meet any inclusion criterion
exclusion.plain: Any unmet item from I-1 to I-6.

exclusion.criterion: Severe medical or psychiatric impairment (e.g., psychosis, severe aggressive behavior, other severe clinical symptoms) needing more intensive care such as day treatment or hospitalization, judged by the research team from parent report or direct observation
exclusion.plain: Check for psychosis, severe aggression, or a current need for day treatment or hospitalization.

screening_notes: The SCQ (parent report, ≥11) is a screening questionnaire.
The research team gives the ADOS-2 (Module 3 or 4) to confirm the language level.
The research team gives the KBIT-2 (verbal IQ of 70 or above).
Parent-report SCARED or PRAS-ASD must show significant elevations. The record does not give specific cutoffs.
The research team decides on severe impairment (E-2) from parent report or direct observation.
The guardian or caregiver must be available to take part in the FYF intervention.
62a85b0d9788c8be2544cbc41aee6c1508010e2e.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
62a85b0d9788c8be2544cbc41aee6c1508010e2e.benefits: The waitlist group can join the FYF intervention after the waiting period. No other benefits (such as cost coverage) are stated in the registry record.
62a85b0d9788c8be2544cbc41aee6c1508010e2e.involves: Random assignment to immediate FYF CBT (with a caregiver) or a waitlist with treatment as usual, then FYF; EEG, anxiety, and other assessments over the study; no placebo; number of visits and duration not stated.

e02ad7f228ab91683f7b8d9318ce127f379130da.overview: This study enrolls adults aged 18-55 with known or suspected temporal lobe epilepsy who are already in the hospital for intracranial electrode monitoring as part of their epilepsy care. Researchers are building CAMERA, a system that combines brain, body, behavior, and environment recordings with ecological momentary assessments (EMAs) and machine learning. The goal is to predict anxiety state and memory performance continuously.

inclusion.criterion: Age 18 Years to 55 Years; any sex
inclusion.plain: Confirm DOB: age 18-55

inclusion.criterion: Known or suspected Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
inclusion.plain: Confirm TLE diagnosis or clinical suspicion of TLE

inclusion.criterion: Native or proficient in speaking English or Spanish
inclusion.plain: Check language: speaks English or Spanish well

inclusion.criterion: sEEG cases: implant plan includes hippocampal head, body, and tail electrodes, unilateral or bilateral
inclusion.plain: Review sEEG implant plan for hippocampal head/body/tail coverage

inclusion.criterion: 7th grade reading level (minimum level considered literate for adults)
inclusion.plain: Confirm reading at 7th grade level or higher

exclusion.criterion: Hearing impaired (i.e., not corrected with a hearing aid)
exclusion.plain: Check for hearing loss that a hearing aid does not correct

exclusion.criterion: Unable to read the newspaper at arm's length with corrective lenses
exclusion.plain: Check that near vision with glasses or lenses is adequate

exclusion.criterion: Objective intellectual impairment (estimated IQ < 70)
exclusion.plain: Look for any IQ estimate < 70 or documented intellectual disability

exclusion.criterion: Any history of Electroconvulsive Therapy or psychosis (except postictal psychosis for patients)
exclusion.plain: Check for any ECT or non-postictal psychosis

exclusion.criterion: Psychotic disorder (lifetime)
exclusion.plain: Check for any lifetime psychotic disorder diagnosis

exclusion.criterion: Current Anxiety disorder, Major Depressive Disorder, or Bipolar Disorder
exclusion.plain: Check for an active anxiety disorder, MDD, or bipolar diagnosis

exclusion.criterion: Neurodegenerative diseases, widespread brain lesions, or language problems (other than naming difficulty)
exclusion.plain: Review neuro history and imaging; naming difficulty alone is allowed

exclusion.criterion: Medical conditions that could affect cognitive performance (e.g., HIV infection, cancer with metastatic potential)
exclusion.plain: Check for HIV, cancer with metastatic potential, or similar conditions

exclusion.criterion: Acute renal failure or end-stage renal disease
exclusion.plain: Check renal history and labs for AKI or ESRD

screening_notes: Reading level (7th grade) needs a screen; the record does not name the test.
Language ability in English or Spanish should be confirmed by interview.
IQ < 70 needs an objective estimate, such as from neuropsych testing.
Current anxiety disorder, MDD, or bipolar disorder, plus lifetime psychosis or psychotic disorder, needs a psychiatric interview or chart review. Postictal psychosis does not exclude.
Hearing (corrected with an aid) and near vision (reading a newspaper at arm's length with corrective lenses) need a bedside check.
sEEG candidates need an implant plan review with the epilepsy or neurosurgery team.
Renal status (acute renal failure or end-stage renal disease) needs a lab or chart review.
e02ad7f228ab91683f7b8d9318ce127f379130da.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
e02ad7f228ab91683f7b8d9318ce127f379130da.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
e02ad7f228ab91683f7b8d9318ce127f379130da.involves: Recording of passive neural, body, behavior, and environment data plus adaptive EMAs during clinical inpatient intracranial monitoring. The record states no study drug, placebo, visit schedule, or duration.

24b4c84e95ef88d698bcec4b5a8863df45721bf6.overview: This trial is for Latino/Hispanic older adults with cancer (OACs), aged 65 or older, who have anxiety (HADS-A ≥6). Their primary informal caregiver, aged 40 or older, can also join. The study is testing whether an anxiety treatment program (MAC) is practical and effective for these patients and caregivers. A patient can enroll without a caregiver.

inclusion.criterion: Registry age limit: 40 years to no max, all sexes
inclusion.plain: Overall age floor is 40; see the separate age rules for patients and caregivers

inclusion.criterion: OAC: age 65 years or older (medical record or self-report)
inclusion.plain: Confirm the patient is 65 or older

inclusion.criterion: OAC: currently on active cancer treatment OR within eighteen months of finishing it (surgery, chemotherapy, radiation, immunotherapy)
inclusion.plain: Check treatment dates: active now, or ended within the last 18 months

inclusion.criterion: OAC: self-identifies as Latino and/or Hispanic ethnicity
inclusion.plain: Confirm ethnicity by self-report

inclusion.criterion: OAC: has a primary informal (unpaid) caregiver aged 40 or older who is willing and able to take part; patients without one can still enroll
inclusion.plain: Ask about a caregiver (optional, not required for the patient to enroll)

inclusion.criterion: OAC: HADS anxiety subscale score ≥6
inclusion.plain: Give the HADS and confirm the anxiety score is ≥6

inclusion.criterion: OAC: fluent in English and/or Spanish (CRC asks 2 questions: speaks it 'very well' or 'well', and prefers English/Spanish for healthcare)
inclusion.plain: CRC checks language fluency before enrollment

inclusion.criterion: Caregiver: named by the OAC as their primary informal (unpaid) caregiver
inclusion.plain: The patient confirms this person is their primary unpaid caregiver

inclusion.criterion: Caregiver: age 40 years or older (self-report)
inclusion.plain: Confirm the caregiver is 40 or older

inclusion.criterion: Caregiver: fluent in English and/or Spanish (same 2-question CRC check)
inclusion.plain: CRC checks language fluency before enrollment

exclusion.criterion: OAC/Caregiver: currently receiving psychotherapy
exclusion.plain: Check whether they are in therapy now

exclusion.criterion: OAC/Caregiver: on psychotropic medication for < 8 weeks before MAC Session 1, and/or expects to change medication during the study
exclusion.plain: Psychotropics must be stable for at least 8 weeks, with no changes planned

exclusion.criterion: OAC/Caregiver: currently treated for schizophrenia, substance use or dependence, and/or bipolar disorder
exclusion.plain: Check the psychiatric history and problem list

exclusion.criterion: OAC/Caregiver: severe cognitive impairment, Blessed Orientation Memory Concentration score ≥ 11
exclusion.plain: Give the BOMC; a score of ≥11 excludes

exclusion.criterion: OAC/Caregiver: too ill or weak to complete study procedures (staff judgment and/or self-report)
exclusion.plain: Judge whether they are well enough to take part

exclusion.criterion: OAC only: receiving hospice care at enrollment
exclusion.plain: Check hospice status

screening_notes: HADS anxiety subscale must be given to the OAC; a score of ≥6 is required
Blessed Orientation Memory Concentration test for both OAC and caregiver; a score of ≥11 excludes
CRC language check (2 questions) for both OAC and caregiver before enrollment
Psychotropic medication history: stable for at least 8 weeks before MAC Session 1, with no changes planned
Staff judgment on whether the person is too ill or weak to take part
Several criteria rely on self-report only, including ethnicity, caregiver status, and caregiver psychiatric history
24b4c84e95ef88d698bcec4b5a8863df45721bf6.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
24b4c84e95ef88d698bcec4b5a8863df45721bf6.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
24b4c84e95ef88d698bcec4b5a8863df45721bf6.involves: Anxiety treatment program (MAC sessions) for the OAC, with an optional caregiver. The record does not state the number of visits, duration, or whether there is a placebo or control group.

c6ccdb53f21607c38516043dcbcaac8f65d65c41.overview: This is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial testing whether ITI-1284 monotherapy is effective, safe and tolerable. It is enrolling adults aged 18 or older (no upper age limit) with current moderate-to-severe GAD under DSM-5-TR. Patients must have responded inadequately to at least 2 approved GAD treatments, but must not have failed more than 3.

inclusion.criterion: Age 18 years or older (no maximum); any sex
inclusion.plain: Confirm the patient is 18 or older

inclusion.criterion: Written informed consent given before any study procedures
inclusion.plain: Patient can and will give written consent

inclusion.criterion: Current moderate or severe GAD by DSM-5-TR, confirmed with SCID-5-CT by the Investigator or a Sponsor-approved rater at Screening
inclusion.plain: Chart shows current GAD diagnosis; severity is confirmed by the site's SCID-5-CT

inclusion.criterion: HAM-A Total score ≥ 22 at Screening and Baseline
inclusion.plain: Measured by the study rater; check recent symptom severity in the chart

inclusion.criterion: HAM-A Items 1 (anxious mood) and 2 (tension) each scored ≥ 2 at Screening and Baseline
inclusion.plain: Measured by the study rater

inclusion.criterion: CGI-S score ≥ 4 at Screening and Baseline
inclusion.plain: At least moderately ill on clinician rating

inclusion.criterion: Inadequate response (< 50% improvement on modified ATRQ for GAD) to ≥ 2 of: paroxetine ≥ 20 mg, venlafaxine XR ≥ 75mg, duloxetine ≥ 60 mg, escitalopram ≥ 10mg, buspirone ≥ 20 mg/day, each for ≥ 6 weeks prior to Screening, taken for ongoing GAD symptoms
inclusion.plain: Check med history for 2 or more adequate dose/duration trials of these specific drugs with < 50% improvement

exclusion.criterion: Lifetime DSM-5-TR schizophrenia, schizoaffective, schizophreniform, or other psychotic disorder
exclusion.plain: Check for any lifetime psychotic disorder diagnosis

exclusion.criterion: Lifetime DSM-5-TR bipolar disorder
exclusion.plain: Check for any bipolar diagnosis

exclusion.criterion: MADRS total score > 18 at Screening or Baseline
exclusion.plain: Significant comorbid depression excludes; study rater scores this

exclusion.criterion: Significant risk of suicidal behavior during the study, in the Investigator's opinion
exclusion.plain: Review current suicide risk

exclusion.criterion: C-SSRS Suicidal Ideation Item 4 or 5 'yes' within 6 months before Screening, or since Screening at Baseline
exclusion.plain: Check for active suicidal ideation with intent or plan in the past 6 months

exclusion.criterion: 1 or more suicide attempts within the 2 years prior to Screening
exclusion.plain: Check for any suicide attempt in the past 2 years

exclusion.criterion: MADRS Item 10 score ≥ 5 at Screening or Baseline
exclusion.plain: Study rater scores this suicidal-thoughts item

exclusion.criterion: Imminent danger to self or others per Investigator assessment
exclusion.plain: Check for current dangerousness

exclusion.criterion: Lifetime failure to respond to > 3 approved GAD treatments (paroxetine 20 mg, venlafaxine XR 75mg, duloxetine 60 mg, escitalopram 10mg, buspirone 20 mg minimum daily dose) for at least 6 weeks each
exclusion.plain: Patients who failed 4 or more of these drugs at adequate dose and duration are excluded

screening_notes: The SCID-5-CT structured interview is needed to confirm moderate or severe GAD
HAM-A (total ≥ 22; Items 1 and 2 each ≥ 2) and CGI-S ≥ 4 must be met at both Screening and Baseline
Modified ATRQ for GAD is used to document < 50% improvement on prior treatments; collect pharmacy and dose records

c6ccdb53f21607c38516043dcbcaac8f65d65c41.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.

127ef605ae1d94cc6ae9ed2b0ac74f384f0513fb.overview: This pilot tests "Maya," a mobile CBT app adapted for stroke, in adults with recent stroke (within 1 month) who screen positive for depression and/or anxiety. It looks at acceptability, feasibility, and early signs of efficacy during acute rehabilitation. Post-stroke neuropsychiatric symptoms are common and linked to poorer recovery and quality of life.

127ef605ae1d94cc6ae9ed2b0ac74f384f0513fb.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.

5fa41761ae2ab48c26f16073b3076de9db647821.overview: Pilot study at MSK testing whether early access to psychiatric care during sarcoma treatment is feasible. It also looks at how early psychiatric referral relates to depression, anxiety, postoperative outcomes, and patient satisfaction. It enrolls adults with newly diagnosed, untreated primary bone or soft tissue sarcoma who are having surgery through Orthopaedic Surgery. Patients are included whatever their baseline level of anxiety or depression symptoms.

inclusion.plain: Confirm patient is 18 or older

inclusion.plain: Check pathology for primary sarcoma, or get PI approval if diagnosis is based on imaging/history only

inclusion.plain: Confirm referral or visit is with Orthopaedic Surgery

inclusion.criterion: No previous treatment for sarcoma
inclusion.plain: Check for any prior sarcoma treatment (surgery, chemo, radiation)

inclusion.plain: Ask the Census-LEP question and confirm English is the preferred language for healthcare

exclusion.plain: Review chart and history for severe mental illness, suicide attempts, or psychiatric admissions

Patients with no or mild anxiety or depression symptoms are deliberately included; do not screen them out.

50149899372027d470e31f75daf57ff0c3fc6d64.overview: This study is for adults with severe, treatment-refractory OCD who have already chosen to get clinically indicated directional DBS of the anterior limb of the internal capsule (ALIC), outside of research. Before surgery, each patient gets a 7T MRI used to plan personalized lead placement along five ALIC white-matter pathways. The aim is to map which pathways give the most benefit for OCD.

840e09d80aff1b2c5a5298cee113d79f2fbf52bb.overview: This is a single-center randomized trial with 52 adults (26 per arm). All participants are having primary THA, TKA, or UKA for osteoarthritis under spinal/regional anesthesia. It tests whether music the patient chooses, played through noise-cancelling headphones in preop holding, lowers acute preoperative anxiety compared with usual care alone. The primary outcome is the change in prorated STAI-6 score (20-80 scale) from arrival in preop holding (T1) to just before OR transport (T2).

7a455b9e13c0458d9903e9fec487cccda8c90d22.involves: Open-label psilocybin 25mg, two doses, no placebo. The record gives the dose gap as both "3-4 weeks apart" and "at least three weeks apart". Follow-up up to 5 weeks: one visit 1 month after the last integration session, with biomarkers.

Biological samples are taken at acute anxiety or depression, then weekly until remission (defined as 6 months symptom-free), and again if symptoms come back. Total length is not stated.

00de75091337b75ebe31e2193da555c5bafd37b5.overview: This RCT enrolls adults aged 18-64 who have type 1 diabetes plus an anxiety or depressive disorder. It tests whether telemedicine-delivered Unified Protocol CBT (UP-CBT) with CGM review improves anxiety/depressive symptoms and glycemic control more than CGM alone. It plans to enroll 94 people nationally, entirely virtually, with targeted recruitment of racial/ethnic minorities.

inclusion.criterion: Type 1 diabetes duration ≥ 6 months
inclusion.plain: Confirm T1D diagnosis date is ≥ 6 months ago

inclusion.criterion: 18-64 years old (Sex: ALL)
inclusion.plain: Check age is 18-64; any sex

inclusion.criterion: English- or Spanish-speaking
inclusion.plain: Confirm patient speaks English or Spanish

inclusion.criterion: Anxiety or depressive mood disorder as per structured diagnostic interview
inclusion.plain: Diagnosis must be confirmed by structured interview, not just a chart diagnosis

exclusion.criterion: Developmental or sensory disability interfering with participation
exclusion.plain: Check for developmental/sensory disability that would stop them taking part

exclusion.criterion: Current pregnancy
exclusion.plain: Check for current pregnancy

exclusion.criterion: Bipolar disorders, psychotic disorders, severe eating disorders, or severe substance abuse disorders
exclusion.plain: Look for bipolar, psychosis, severe ED, or severe SUD diagnoses

exclusion.criterion: Acute suicidal risk or self-harm
exclusion.plain: Check for current suicidal risk or self-harm

exclusion.criterion: Medications or recent medical procedures that would impact glycemic control or CGM use over the study
exclusion.plain: Review meds and recent procedures that affect glucose or CGM wear

exclusion.criterion: Received CBT in last year or plans to initiate CBT
exclusion.plain: Check for CBT in the past 12 months or planned CBT

exclusion.criterion: Temporary: recent psychotropic initiation; must be on stable dose for 6 weeks prior to enrollment
exclusion.plain: Confirm psychotropic dose unchanged for 6 weeks; if not, defer enrollment

screening_notes: I-4 needs a structured diagnostic interview to confirm an anxiety or depressive disorder.
E-3/E-4 need a psychiatric screen for bipolar disorder, psychosis, eating disorder or substance use disorder severity, and acute suicide/self-harm risk.
E-7 needs the psychotropic start date and the date of the last dose change (6-week stable-dose rule).
E-5 needs a medication and procedure review for anything affecting glycemic control or CGM use.
Pregnancy status must be checked (E-2).
The description says 'suboptimally controlled' T1D, but the eligibility text gives no HbA1c threshold. Confirm any glycemic cutoff with the study team.
Separate qualitative component: 2-4 focus groups of people with T1D aged 35-64.
00de75091337b75ebe31e2193da555c5bafd37b5.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
00de75091337b75ebe31e2193da555c5bafd37b5.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
00de75091337b75ebe31e2193da555c5bafd37b5.involves: Randomized to telemedicine UP-CBT + CGM review or CGM alone (no placebo). The study is fully virtual and lasts 12 months, with HbA1c, patient-reported outcome surveys, and smartphone EMA linked to CGM data.

c6390bca51400e8de341bc4203806939d249387b.overview: This trial is for adults (18 or older, no upper age limit, any sex) with chronic, severe, treatment-resistant OCD. They are offered deep brain stimulation (DBS) instead of irreversible ablative surgery such as anterior capsulotomy. The record says it does not test efficacy. Candidates must meet the insurance criteria for coverage of the implanted system.

inclusion.criterion: Diagnosis of OCD with a documented duration of at least 5 years
inclusion.plain: Confirm OCD diagnosis and records showing it has lasted 5 years or more

inclusion.criterion: OCD rated as severe or extreme illness
inclusion.plain: Check the documented severity rating is severe or extreme

inclusion.criterion: Failed to improve after at least 3 SSRIs and clomipramine
inclusion.plain: Check medication history: 3 or more SSRIs plus clomipramine, without improvement

inclusion.criterion: Hoarding is not the primary subclassification
inclusion.plain: Confirm the main OCD subtype is not hoarding

inclusion.criterion: Completed or tried to complete Exposure and Response Prevention Therapy (ERP)
inclusion.plain: Check for a completed or attempted course of ERP

inclusion.criterion: No serious psychiatric disorder besides OCD (e.g. comorbid personality disorder) and no current substance abuse
inclusion.plain: Check for comorbid serious psychiatric diagnoses and current substance abuse

inclusion.criterion: Meets established criteria for implantation of a DBS system
inclusion.plain: Confirm the patient is a candidate for DBS implantation

inclusion.criterion: Age 18 years or older; any sex
inclusion.plain: Check age is 18 or older

inclusion.criterion: No previous surgery to destroy the brain region that will be the stimulation target
inclusion.plain: Check for prior ablative surgery (e.g. capsulotomy) at the target

inclusion.criterion: Not pregnant
inclusion.plain: Confirm pregnancy status

inclusion.criterion: No other neurological disorders, including dementia
inclusion.plain: Check for neurological diagnoses or dementia

inclusion.criterion: No bleeding disorder and not taking blood thinners
inclusion.plain: Check for coagulopathy and anticoagulant or antiplatelet use

inclusion.criterion: Capable of giving informed consent
inclusion.plain: Confirm the patient has capacity to consent

exclusion.criterion: Unable to properly operate the neurostimulator
exclusion.plain: Judge whether the patient can manage the device controls

exclusion.criterion: Will be exposed to diathermy
exclusion.plain: Check for expected or planned diathermy exposure

screening_notes: Severity rating (severe or extreme) needs a clinical assessment; the record does not name a scale
Ruling out serious psychiatric comorbidity, including personality disorder, and current substance abuse needs a psychiatric interview
Confirm DBS candidacy with the neurosurgeon
Check the ERP history (completed or attempted) and the full medication history with the patient
Do a pregnancy test where relevant
Check coagulation status and anticoagulant use before surgery
Insurance coverage of the device must be obtained for enrollment
Capacity to consent and ability to operate the neurostimulator need a manual check
c6390bca51400e8de341bc4203806939d249387b.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
c6390bca51400e8de341bc4203806939d249387b.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
c6390bca51400e8de341bc4203806939d249387b.involves: Open-label DBS: lead placed in the brain by stereotactic surgery, plus a neurostimulator implanted in the subclavicular region. Follow-up with psychiatry and neurosurgery at 2 weeks and 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 months, then every 6 months. No placebo. Coverage through insurance is required.

1de5da78699b4f4c44b14a8e3f450f3ef25c6af8.overview: This is an exploratory, decentralized, single-arm, open-label study of Neuralli Mood, a probiotic/postbiotic supplement (L. plantarum PS128 + heat-treated L. paracasei PS23). It enrolls generally healthy adults aged 18 and older with stress, occasional sleep disruption, low mood, anxiety symptoms, or work burnout. Participants act as their own controls, rating stress, sleep, mood, anxiety, depression, happiness, and burnout themselves before and after 90 days of use.

inclusion.criterion: Age 18 years or older (no upper limit), any sex, able to provide informed consent
inclusion.plain: Confirm age ≥18 and capacity to consent

inclusion.criterion: Generally healthy adult with stress, occasional sleep disruption, low mood, anxiety symptoms, or work-related burnout
inclusion.plain: Confirm generally healthy with at least one of these complaints

inclusion.criterion: Willing and able to take two capsules of Neuralli Mood daily for 90 days
inclusion.plain: Patient agrees to 90 days of daily dosing

inclusion.criterion: Willing and able to complete electronic baseline, follow-up, adherence, and safety assessments
inclusion.plain: Patient can complete online questionnaires

inclusion.criterion: Reliable internet access and an email-enabled device
inclusion.plain: Ask the patient about internet and email access

exclusion.criterion: Pregnant or nursing
exclusion.plain: Check pregnancy and breastfeeding status

exclusion.criterion: Known allergy/hypersensitivity to Neuralli Mood, probiotics, or any ingredient
exclusion.plain: Review the allergy list for probiotics and product ingredients

exclusion.criterion: Severe or unstable GI disease, including conditions where probiotics may be inappropriate
exclusion.plain: Review GI history (e.g., active or unstable GI disease)

exclusion.criterion: Immunocompromised status or current immunosuppressive therapy
exclusion.plain: Check for immunodeficiency or immunosuppressant medications

exclusion.criterion: Severe or unstable mood disorder, acute psychiatric symptoms, or current risk of harm to self/others
exclusion.plain: Check psychiatric stability; screen for suicidal or homicidal risk

exclusion.criterion: Clinically significant sleep disorder needing management by a healthcare professional
exclusion.plain: Rule out diagnosed significant sleep disorders (e.g., OSA, narcolepsy)

exclusion.criterion: Cognitive impairment or other condition preventing consent or reliable completion of procedures
exclusion.plain: Check for cognitive impairment or inability to complete tasks

exclusion.criterion: History of severe allergic reaction where the investigator judges probiotic use an unacceptable risk
exclusion.plain: Note any anaphylaxis history so the investigator can review it

exclusion.criterion: Medication or medical condition for which a clinician advises against probiotics
exclusion.plain: Review medications and conditions for probiotic contraindications

exclusion.criterion: Any other circumstance making participation inappropriate or unsafe per the investigator
exclusion.plain: Investigator's discretion

screening_notes: Psychiatric interview: confirm mood/anxiety is not severe or unstable, no acute symptoms, and no current risk of harm to self or others (E-5).
Sleep history: separate occasional sleep disruption (eligible) from a clinically significant sleep disorder (excluded) (E-6).
Review medications and history for immunosuppression, GI disease, and probiotic contraindications (E-3, E-4, E-9).
Pregnancy and nursing status must be checked; the record doesn't say whether a pregnancy test is required (E-1).
Check capacity to consent and cognitive status (I-1, E-7).
Severe allergy history needs the investigator's risk judgment (E-8).
The study is decentralized: confirm the patient has internet access and can do electronic assessments (I-4, I-5).
1de5da78699b4f4c44b14a8e3f450f3ef25c6af8.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
1de5da78699b4f4c44b14a8e3f450f3ef25c6af8.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
1de5da78699b4f4c44b14a8e3f450f3ef25c6af8.involves: Neuralli Mood, two capsules once daily for 90 days (30 billion CFU L. plantarum PS128 + 20 billion heat-treated L. paracasei PS23 per dose). Open-label with no placebo and fully remote: electronic questionnaires at baseline and day 90, plus scheduled check-ins on adherence and safety.

2cfbdf7498b39a903220fabb99df619fc0cb15fe.overview: This Phase 2 placebo-controlled trial tests NTX-1472, a new V1a receptor antagonist, in adults aged 18–65 with generalized Social Anxiety Disorder (SAD). It is looking at safety, tolerability and how well the drug works. Candidates need clinically significant social anxiety (LSAS ≥70), must not be markedly depressed, and must not be on daily psychotropics.

inclusion.criterion: Written informed consent; willing to comply with all protocol requirements
inclusion.plain: Patient agrees to consent and can follow the protocol

inclusion.criterion: English speaker
inclusion.plain: Confirm the patient speaks English

inclusion.criterion: Male or female, ≥18 and ≤65 years of age
inclusion.plain: Check age is 18–65

inclusion.criterion: Current generalized SAD per DSM-5, confirmed by SCID-5-CT
inclusion.plain: Has a generalized SAD diagnosis; SCID-5-CT done at screening

inclusion.criterion: Clinician-administered LSAS total score ≥70 at Screening
inclusion.plain: LSAS ≥70, scored at screening

inclusion.criterion: Clinician-rated HDRS-17 total score <16 at Screening
inclusion.plain: HDRS-17 under 16 at screening

inclusion.criterion: If of childbearing potential: effective birth control during study and at least 14 days after last dose
inclusion.plain: Patient agrees to use contraception through 14 days after the last dose

exclusion.criterion: Current performance-only SAD per DSM-5, confirmed by SCID-5-CT
exclusion.plain: Rule out performance-only SAD subtype

exclusion.criterion: Current ADHD, autism spectrum disorder, MDD, personality disorder, or PTSD (current GAD allowed)
exclusion.plain: No current ADHD, ASD, MDD, personality disorder or PTSD; GAD is OK

exclusion.criterion: Past or current bipolar, adult feeding/eating disorder, OCD, schizophrenia spectrum/psychotic disorder; substance use disorder within 12 months of Screening
exclusion.plain: Check lifetime history for these; SUD only counts if within 12 months

exclusion.criterion: Receiving daily psychotropics within 4 weeks of Screening
exclusion.plain: No daily psychotropic medication in the 4 weeks before screening

exclusion.criterion: At risk for suicidal ideation per C-SSRS
exclusion.plain: C-SSRS shows no suicide risk

exclusion.criterion: Moderate or severe hepatic impairment
exclusion.plain: Check liver function/history

exclusion.criterion: Severe renal impairment
exclusion.plain: Check renal function

exclusion.criterion: Pregnant, or breastfeeding unless willing to stop for study duration
exclusion.plain: Not pregnant; if breastfeeding, willing to stop for the study

screening_notes: SCID-5-CT interview needed to confirm generalized SAD (not performance-only) and to screen for comorbid diagnoses
Clinician-administered LSAS at screening (needs ≥70)
Clinician-rated HDRS-17 at screening (needs <16)
C-SSRS suicide risk assessment
Medication review for any daily psychotropic within 4 weeks of screening; may require washout
Labs for hepatic and renal function; pregnancy status for patients of childbearing potential
Substance use history for the 12 months before screening
2cfbdf7498b39a903220fabb99df619fc0cb15fe.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
2cfbdf7498b39a903220fabb99df619fc0cb15fe.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
2cfbdf7498b39a903220fabb99df619fc0cb15fe.involves: NTX-1472 or matching placebo capsule daily for 8 weeks; 6 clinic visits over 14 weeks.

eca88059dacc1404749f600109af2f0d924aa1a6.overview: The trial is looking for adults with current moderate or severe GAD (DSM-5-TR) who are not responding well enough to an FDA-approved GAD treatment they are taking now. They must also have had an inadequate response to a different approved GAD treatment in the past. The study tests whether adding ITI-1284 to their current treatment works better than adding placebo, and how safe and tolerable it is.

inclusion.criterion: Written informed consent before any study-specific procedures
inclusion.plain: Patient is able and willing to give written consent

inclusion.criterion: Male or female, ≥ 18 years of age (no upper age limit)
inclusion.plain: Confirm age ≥ 18; any sex

inclusion.criterion: Meets DSM-5-TR criteria for current moderate or severe GAD, confirmed by SCID-5-CT (Investigator or Sponsor-approved rater)
inclusion.plain: Confirm current moderate or severe GAD diagnosis; the study does the structured interview

inclusion.criterion: HAM-A Total score ≥ 22 at Screening and Baseline
inclusion.plain: Rated by study staff at both visits

inclusion.criterion: HAM-A Items 1 (anxious mood) and 2 (tension) each ≥ 2 at Screening and Baseline
inclusion.plain: Rated by study staff at both visits

inclusion.criterion: CGI-S ≥ 4 at Screening and Baseline
inclusion.plain: At least moderately ill on clinician rating

inclusion.criterion: History of inadequate response (< 50% improvement on modified ATRQ for GAD) to ≥ 1 approved GAD treatment at adequate dose (paroxetine 20 mg, venlafaxine XR 75 mg, duloxetine 60 mg, escitalopram 10 mg, buspirone 20 mg minimum total daily) taken daily for at least 6 weeks
inclusion.plain: Check chart for a past trial of one of these drugs at or above minimum dose for ≥ 6 weeks with < 50% improvement

inclusion.criterion: Currently inadequate response to paroxetine, venlafaxine XR, duloxetine, escitalopram, or buspirone at adequate dose (same minimums) for ≥ 6 weeks before Screening; agrees to keep the same regimen through the study
inclusion.plain: Current drug is at or above minimum dose for ≥ 6 weeks with ongoing symptoms; no dose changes planned

inclusion.criterion: Current GAD treatment must be different from the GAD treatment identified as the historical failure
inclusion.plain: Current drug ≠ the drug that failed in the past

exclusion.criterion: Lifetime confirmed DSM-5-TR schizophrenia, schizoaffective, schizophreniform or other psychotic disorder, or bipolar disorder
exclusion.plain: Check full psychiatric history for any psychotic or bipolar diagnosis

exclusion.criterion: MADRS total score > 18 at Screening or Baseline
exclusion.plain: Significant comorbid depressive symptoms exclude; rated by the study

exclusion.criterion: Significant suicide risk in the Investigator's opinion
exclusion.plain: Review suicide risk history

exclusion.criterion: C-SSRS Suicidal Ideation Items 4 or 5 'yes' within 6 months before Screening, or since Screening at Baseline
exclusion.plain: Any active suicidal ideation with intent or plan in the past 6 months

exclusion.criterion: 1 or more suicide attempts within the 2 years before Screening
exclusion.plain: Check chart for suicide attempts in the last 2 years

exclusion.criterion: MADRS Item 10 score ≥ 5 at Screening or Baseline
exclusion.plain: Rated by the study

exclusion.criterion: Imminent danger to self or others per Investigator
exclusion.plain: Clinical judgment of acute risk

exclusion.criterion: Lifetime failure to respond to > 3 approved GAD treatments (paroxetine, venlafaxine XR, duloxetine, escitalopram, buspirone) at adequate dose (same minimums) and duration (≥ 6 weeks)
exclusion.plain: Count adequate failed trials of these 5 drugs; more than 3 excludes

screening_notes: SCID-5-CT interview to confirm DSM-5-TR GAD diagnosis and severity (Investigator or Sponsor-approved rater)
HAM-A (total ≥ 22; Items 1 and 2 ≥ 2) and CGI-S (≥ 4) must be met at both Screening and Baseline
MADRS total (> 18 excludes) and Item 10 (≥ 5 excludes) at Screening and Baseline
C-SSRS at Screening (6-month lookback) and Baseline (since Screening)
Modified ATRQ for GAD to document past and current inadequate response (< 50% improvement)
Pharmacy/chart check of drug, dose, and ≥ 6-week duration for both the past and current GAD treatments; they must be different drugs
Count of lifetime adequate failed GAD trials (> 3 excludes)
The registry age field lists no minimum, but inclusion criterion 2 requires age ≥ 18
eca88059dacc1404749f600109af2f0d924aa1a6.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
eca88059dacc1404749f600109af2f0d924aa1a6.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
eca88059dacc1404749f600109af2f0d924aa1a6.involves: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial: ITI-1284 or placebo added to the current GAD drug, which stays at the same dose. Visit schedule and study length are not stated.

4737f453891d8a80c84cbf44f956c5cde74a14d7.overview: This is a single-site randomized pilot at Mount Sinai Hospital. It wants adult women (obstetric patients) who are having an ultrasound-guided needle procedure. It tests whether virtual reality reduces pain and anxiety during the procedure compared with standard care.

inclusion.criterion: Female, age ≥18 (no upper age limit)
inclusion.plain: Confirm female sex and age ≥18

inclusion.criterion: English-speaking
inclusion.plain: Confirm English language proficiency

inclusion.criterion: Undergoing ultrasound-guided needle procedure at Mount Sinai
inclusion.plain: Confirm a scheduled US-guided obstetric needle procedure at Mount Sinai

exclusion.criterion: History of seizures
exclusion.plain: Check history for any seizure disorder or past seizures

exclusion.criterion: Severe motion sickness
exclusion.plain: Ask about or check for severe motion sickness

screening_notes: Ask the patient directly about severe motion sickness. The chart may not record it.
Check seizure history by reviewing the chart and asking the patient.
Confirm English-speaking status at intake.
4737f453891d8a80c84cbf44f956c5cde74a14d7.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
4737f453891d8a80c84cbf44f956c5cde74a14d7.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
4737f453891d8a80c84cbf44f956c5cde74a14d7.involves: Patients are randomly assigned to VR or standard care during a single US-guided needle procedure, then complete questionnaires on pain, anxiety, acceptability and satisfaction. No placebo is used, and no other visits or follow-up are described.

30fb1d063a2173ea17849d0319faa7a7735e0116.overview: This trial is for adults aged 18 to 74 with DSM-5-TR Generalized Anxiety Disorder. It tests whether a single and/or repeat dose of RE104 for Injection reduces anxiety symptoms compared with placebo.

inclusion.criterion: Age 18 Years to 74 Years, any sex
inclusion.plain: Confirm the patient's age is between 18 and 74

inclusion.criterion: Generalized Anxiety Disorder as defined by DSM-5-TR
inclusion.plain: Confirm there is a documented DSM-5-TR GAD diagnosis

inclusion.criterion: Females: not pregnant or planning pregnancy; males: not planning to make a partner pregnant
inclusion.plain: Check pregnancy status and plans to conceive

inclusion.criterion: Willing and able to comply with study conditions and requirements
inclusion.plain: Ask whether the patient can and will follow study requirements

exclusion.criterion: Significant risk of suicide
exclusion.plain: Check the chart for current suicide risk

exclusion.criterion: Active or past bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, psychotic disorder and/or borderline personality disorder; or a first-degree relative with psychosis or bipolar disorder
exclusion.plain: Check psychiatric history and family history in first-degree relatives

exclusion.criterion: Another concurrent psychiatric disorder that is the primary disorder
exclusion.plain: Confirm GAD is the primary diagnosis

exclusion.criterion: Other medically significant conditions that make the patient unsuitable
exclusion.plain: Review medical comorbidities

exclusion.criterion: Has used or will need prohibited medications or therapies
exclusion.plain: Review current and past medications and therapies (the prohibited list is not given in the record)

exclusion.criterion: Known sensitivity or intolerance to the study intervention or potential rescue medications
exclusion.plain: Check allergies and intolerances

screening_notes: Suicide risk needs a clinical assessment; the record does not name a scale or cutoff.
Confirm the DSM-5-TR GAD diagnosis and that GAD is the primary disorder through a clinical interview.
Take a personal and first-degree family history of psychosis and bipolar disorder.
The record does not list the prohibited medications/therapies or the rescue medications; get these from the study team.
Pregnancy status and plans need checking; the record does not say whether a pregnancy test is required.
The record does not define 'medically significant conditions'; the study team decides who is suitable.
30fb1d063a2173ea17849d0319faa7a7735e0116.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
30fb1d063a2173ea17849d0319faa7a7735e0116.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
30fb1d063a2173ea17849d0319faa7a7735e0116.involves: Single and/or repeat dose of RE104 for Injection vs placebo; the record does not give the number of visits or study length.

0cf934dd54e8da1320270160a16e27ad7dad3a72.overview: This trial is for adults aged 18 to 80 who have had DSM-5-TR Adjustment Disorder, with depressed mood or with mixed anxiety and depressed mood, for at least 4 weeks. The disorder must have been triggered by cancer, ALS, MS, PD or IPF. It tests whether a single dose of RE104 for Injection reduces depressive symptoms, or mixed depressive and anxiety symptoms, compared with an active placebo.

inclusion.criterion: ≥4 week history of AjD (DSM-5-TR), with depressed mood or mixed anxiety and depressed mood, confirmed by clinical interview
inclusion.plain: Confirm AjD subtype and that it has lasted ≥4 weeks

inclusion.criterion: Willing and able to comply with study conditions and requirements
inclusion.plain: Assess willingness and ability to comply

exclusion.criterion: Significant risk of suicide
exclusion.plain: Review suicide risk

exclusion.criterion: Active/history of bipolar, schizophrenia, schizoaffective, psychotic or borderline personality disorder; or first-degree family history of psychosis or bipolar disorder
exclusion.plain: Review psychiatric history and first-degree family history

exclusion.plain: Check for any current or past CNS tumor, including in cancer patients

exclusion.criterion: Other medically significant conditions making the patient unsuitable
exclusion.plain: Review comorbidities

exclusion.plain: Check medication list against the protocol's prohibited list

exclusion.criterion: Known sensitivity/intolerance to study intervention or potential rescue medications
exclusion.plain: Review allergies and drug intolerances

screening_notes: AjD diagnosis, subtype and triggering illness must be confirmed by clinical interview
Suicide risk assessment needed; the record does not give a threshold or scale
Cognitive function must be assessed; the record does not name a tool or cutoff

Ask about first-degree family history of psychosis or bipolar disorder
Check pregnancy status and plans
0cf934dd54e8da1320270160a16e27ad7dad3a72.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
0cf934dd54e8da1320270160a16e27ad7dad3a72.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
0cf934dd54e8da1320270160a16e27ad7dad3a72.involves: A single dose of RE104 for Injection compared with an active placebo. The record does not state the number of visits or how long the study lasts.

b7eba033f92c5f89bbe6ef2b13097a7bb23315bc.overview: This is a global, phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial at multiple centers. It is looking for adults aged 18 or older, with no upper age limit, whose primary diagnosis is generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) under DSM-5. It compares the efficacy, safety and tolerability of a fixed dose of SEP-363856 (75 mg/day) with placebo over 8 weeks.

inclusion.plain: Confirm age ≥18 at consent

inclusion.criterion: Primary DSM-5 GAD diagnosis, confirmed by MINI and clinical psychiatric evaluation
inclusion.plain: Documented primary GAD; MINI to be done at screening

inclusion.criterion: BMI 18-40 kg/m^2

inclusion.criterion: Females of childbearing potential: negative pregnancy test plus acceptable contraception; males: follow protocol contraception/reproductive restrictions

exclusion.criterion: Current DSM-5 major depressive episode, PTSD, or any non-GAD psychiatric disorder that was the primary focus of treatment within 12 months before screening
exclusion.plain: Check for current MDE/PTSD or other primary psychiatric treatment focus in past 12 months

exclusion.plain: Check for SUD diagnosis in past 12 months

exclusion.criterion: Lifetime history of certain psychiatric disorders (e.g., schizophrenia spectrum, bipolar, OCD, borderline or antisocial personality disorder)

exclusion.plain: Check for recent SI/suicidal behavior

exclusion.plain: Review recent antipsychotic, mood stabilizer, benzodiazepine, and investigational treatment use

exclusion.criterion: Prior exposure to restricted treatments
exclusion.plain: Check past treatments against the protocol's restricted list

exclusion.criterion: Pregnant or breastfeeding
exclusion.plain: Confirm not pregnant or breastfeeding

exclusion.criterion: Another investigational study within 180 days (or >1 trial in last year)
exclusion.plain: Ask about recent trial participation

exclusion.criterion: Known HIV seropositivity, hepatitis B or C

04fdf996475450d2991613367ab2c53be6d84824.overview: The trial is recruiting young adults aged 18–25 who had early life adversity (ELA), have moderate-to-high stress or trait anxiety, and have no current psychiatric diagnosis. It uses neuroimaging, metabolic, hormonal and behavioural measures to see how oral cannabidiol (CBD) changes the stress response. The aim is to understand how CBD works, as groundwork for treating stress-related disorders early.

inclusion.criterion: Able to understand and give informed consent
inclusion.plain: Has capacity to consent

inclusion.criterion: Age 18 to 25 years; all sexes, with 50% of recruits female to allow sex comparisons
inclusion.plain: Check date of birth; aged 18–25

inclusion.criterion: English speaker
inclusion.plain: Speaks English

inclusion.criterion: MoCA score greater than or equal to 23
inclusion.plain: MoCA ≥23 (study assesses)

inclusion.plain: History of childhood maltreatment, confirmed by MACE/CTQ

exclusion.criterion: Non-medication treatment for anxiety/stress (e.g., CBT) in past three months
exclusion.plain: No psychotherapy for anxiety/stress in last 3 months

exclusion.criterion: Contraindication to CBD (e.g., cannabinoid hypersensitivity) or to product ingredients (sesame oil)
exclusion.plain: Check allergies to cannabinoids and sesame

exclusion.criterion: Pregnant or breastfeeding
exclusion.plain: Pregnancy/lactation status

screening_notes: Study team runs the rating scales: MoCA (≥23), MACE/CTQ for ELA, PSS (≥14)/STAI trait (≥40), GAD-7 (max. 14)
M.I.N.I. 7.2 structured interview to rule out any current DSM-5 diagnosis
Urine drug screen at every visit, plus breathalyzer and timeline follow back; urine also tested for cannabis/CBD
Prescreening labs/ECG: AST/ALT, bilirubin, eGFR, QTc
Pregnancy/lactation and contraception check
Medication review: psychotropics within 3 months, CBD-interacting drugs/supplements/grapefruit within 14 days
Clinician/PI assessment of suicidal/homicidal ideation and overall safety
04fdf996475450d2991613367ab2c53be6d84824.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.

b2cd34bddbbcabdbe2b94b0dbb326f51993f2fec.overview: This is a single-arm pilot of MAYA, a mobile CBT app for adults aged 40 and older whose primary diagnosis is an anxiety or depressive disorder. The main question is whether people will use the app (completed sessions) and how they rate it. It also looks at whether depression and anxiety symptoms go down. The rationale is that older adults often have trouble getting to in-person therapy.

inclusion.criterion: Age 40 or older (all sexes; no upper age limit)
inclusion.plain: Confirm DOB shows age ≥40

inclusion.plain: Primary anxiety/depressive diagnosis; ADIS CSR ≥4 is confirmed at study interview

exclusion.plain: Check for any psychotherapy started in the last 12 weeks

exclusion.criterion: Intent or plan to attempt suicide

screening_notes: ADIS structured interview is needed to confirm primary diagnosis and CSR ≥4
MMSE (in person or remote, remote converted to standard score) compared against age/education norms (≤1 SD below mean)
Suicide risk assessment for intent or plan
Medication and psychotherapy history over the past 12 weeks, plus current CBT status, must be confirmed with the patient
b2cd34bddbbcabdbe2b94b0dbb326f51993f2fec.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
b2cd34bddbbcabdbe2b94b0dbb326f51993f2fec.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
b2cd34bddbbcabdbe2b94b0dbb326f51993f2fec.involves: MAYA CBT app at least 2 days/week, at least 20 min/day, for 6 weeks. Weekly check-ins in person or by Zoom. Assessments at baseline, week 3, week 6 and week 12. Optional EEG at baseline and week 6. Single arm, no control or placebo, 12 weeks total.

cc02f98b321e665edba6df741c59969acc099556.overview: The trial is looking for adults aged 18 or older who have had cancer and have clinically significant anxiety (HADS anxiety ≥8, lasting at least 1 month). It randomizes them to virtual music therapy (MT) or virtual cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to compare how well each reduces anxiety, and looks at whether things like age, sex, race, education and expectations of therapy predict response. It also has two sub-studies with their own criteria: an advanced cancer sub-study (N=50) and a group MT sub-study (N=18).

inclusion.criterion: English- or Spanish-speaking
inclusion.plain: Check preferred language (main study only; both sub-studies are English only)

inclusion.criterion: 18 years or older; any sex
inclusion.plain: Confirm age ≥18

inclusion.criterion: Prior cancer diagnosis of any type or stage
inclusion.plain: Confirm documented cancer history

inclusion.criterion: Advanced sub-study: willing to follow all study procedures; access to Zoom and a quiet/private location
inclusion.plain: Confirm willingness and video access

inclusion.plain: English only; prior cancer, NED/stable, HADS anxiety ≥8, symptoms ≥1 month, Zoom access

exclusion.criterion: Completed active cancer treatment (surgery, radiation, chemotherapy) less than one month before enrollment; maintenance hormonal or targeted therapy allowed

cc02f98b321e665edba6df741c59969acc099556.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.

6a4e5d834148cf8c660a854f61fa1bc74126e61d.overview: This pilot RCT tests whether two mind-body resilience programs, RT-CA 1 and RT-CA 2, are feasible and acceptable for cardiac arrest survivors and their informal caregivers. It plans to enroll 42 dyads (84 participants). It is looking for survivor-caregiver pairs where at least one person has clinically significant emotional distress, and the results will be used to refine the interventions.

inclusion.criterion: Out-of-hospital or in-hospital CA survivor with a new EMR diagnosis of "cardiac arrest" from the index hospitalization and documented loss of pulse
inclusion.plain: Check that the index admission EMR has a new cardiac arrest diagnosis and documented pulselessness

inclusion.criterion: Survivor has an identified caregiver (named by the survivor as their primary source of emotional and functional support)
inclusion.plain: Confirm the survivor names a primary support person who will enroll as the dyad partner

inclusion.criterion: Able and willing to take part in a hybrid in-person/live video intervention
inclusion.plain: Confirm the dyad can do bedside sessions and then Zoom sessions after discharge

inclusion.criterion: English-speaking adults (18 years or older); age 18 years to no maximum, all sexes
inclusion.plain: Check that both members are 18 or older and speak English

inclusion.criterion: At least one dyad member scores >7 on either HADS subscale (anxiety or depression) at screening
inclusion.plain: Give the HADS to both members; at least one must score >7 on either subscale

exclusion.criterion: Active psychosis, mania, substance dependence, or suicidal intent or plan that would require a higher level of care
exclusion.plain: Screen both members for acute psychiatric risk that needs a higher level of care

exclusion.criterion: Any other psychiatric or neurological condition that would preclude meaningful participation
exclusion.plain: Check the chart for conditions (e.g., anoxic brain injury) that would block meaningful participation

exclusion.criterion: Caregiver is a cardiac arrest survivor
exclusion.plain: Confirm the caregiver has no history of cardiac arrest

HADS for both members (at least one must score >7 on either subscale)
Clinical interview of both members for psychosis, mania, substance dependence, and suicidal intent or plan
Clinician judgment needed on other psychiatric or neurological conditions that would block participation
Check the EMR for a new cardiac arrest diagnosis and documented loss of pulse
Ask the survivor to name a caregiver, and confirm the caregiver is not a cardiac arrest survivor
Confirm both members can use Zoom after discharge
6a4e5d834148cf8c660a854f61fa1bc74126e61d.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
6a4e5d834148cf8c660a854f61fa1bc74126e61d.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
6a4e5d834148cf8c660a854f61fa1bc74126e61d.involves: Dyads are randomized to RT-CA 1 (six weekly 30-minute sessions, starting at the ICU or step-down bedside and moving to Zoom after discharge) or RT-CA 2 (one 30-minute bedside session). Surveys at baseline, 6 weeks, and 3 months. No placebo.

87935c322d045ef5d0e82c356b01ad7b2d86d16f.overview: TRIAGE-Psych is a survey study for adults aged 18 and older. It checks whether a person is eligible to be screened for industry-sponsored psychiatry clinical trials. The record gives no description beyond this summary.

87935c322d045ef5d0e82c356b01ad7b2d86d16f.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.

bb922b46c68adfce8e9648ab74ca2c60158e0f30.overview: This randomized trial enrolls 40 unemployed adults in New York State whose primary diagnosis is OCD and who want competitive employment. Everyone gets ERP/CBT. Participants are then randomized to add either Individual Placement and Support (IPS) or standard vocational services (SVS). The goal is to compare work and clinical outcomes between the two employment models.

inclusion.criterion: Age 18 Years to 60 Years, any sex
inclusion.plain: Confirm age is 18-60

inclusion.criterion: Currently unemployed and interested in finding competitive employment in New York State
inclusion.plain: Confirm patient is unemployed and wants competitive work in NY

inclusion.criterion: Primary diagnosis of OCD

Disability benefit status and supported employment status should be confirmed with the patient
Patient's interest in competitive employment and willingness to keep medications stable should be confirmed in an interview
bb922b46c68adfce8e9648ab74ca2c60158e0f30.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.

bb922b46c68adfce8e9648ab74ca2c60158e0f30.involves: Up to 12 ERP/CBT sessions, randomized 1:1 to added IPS or SVS, with no placebo. Assessments happen at baseline, end of CBT, and 6, 9, and 12 months (12-month follow-up).

It enrolls sedentary adults aged 18-50 of any sex in two groups: people with a primary anxiety disorder (GAD, social anxiety disorder or panic disorder) and non-psychiatric controls.
