The study's own screening measures cover anxiety, mood, and trauma.
2cc4ff1afe364b098f4b091664b8e6becb8e2f67.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
2cc4ff1afe364b098f4b091664b8e6becb8e2f67.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
2cc4ff1afe364b098f4b091664b8e6becb8e2f67.involves: Participants complete the 12-module CBT skills app, a daily symptom tracker, symptom measures, app feedback questionnaires, and feedback interviews by phone or video. There is no placebo or control arm, and the study duration is not stated.

a46c3e28a7d2d969fb61f85349bb1fa31612174a.overview: This is a single-arm pilot study in adults aged 40-79 who had a stroke at least 1 month ago and now have clinically significant anxiety and/or depression. It is testing whether "MAYA", a mobile CBT app, is feasible (measured by sessions completed) and acceptable (measured by uMARS scores). It also looks for early signs of benefit on MADRS, HAM-A, and DASS-21 scores.

inclusion.criterion: Age 40-79 (listed as both an inclusion criterion and the demographic limit: 40 Years to 79 Years; all sexes)
inclusion.plain: Confirm DOB: age 40-79

inclusion.criterion: Clinically-significant anxiety and/or depression (as determined by an eligibility evaluation)
inclusion.plain: Study evaluation confirms clinically significant anxiety and/or depression

inclusion.criterion: Stroke that occurred 1 month or more prior to study initiation
inclusion.plain: Check stroke date: 1 month or more before study start

inclusion.criterion: Capacity to provide consent
inclusion.plain: Patient can give their own consent

inclusion.criterion: No greater than mild cognitive difficulties based on study eligibility evaluation
inclusion.plain: Cognitive impairment no worse than mild on the study evaluation

inclusion.criterion: If on depression/anxiety medication, stable dose for a minimum of 8 weeks prior to study initiation
inclusion.plain: Check medication list: no dose changes to antidepressants or anxiolytics in the last 8 weeks

inclusion.criterion: Ability to use iPhone or iPad independently
inclusion.plain: Can use an iPhone or iPad without help

inclusion.criterion: Home internet access
inclusion.plain: Has internet at home

inclusion.criterion: Willingness to participate in the full study duration
inclusion.plain: Willing to take part for all 8 weeks

exclusion.criterion: Aphasia of moderate or greater severity (as determined during eligibility evaluation)
exclusion.plain: Check for moderate or worse aphasia

exclusion.criterion: Non-fluency in English
exclusion.plain: Confirm the patient is fluent in English

exclusion.criterion: History of a bipolar or psychotic disorder
exclusion.plain: Check the problem list for any history of bipolar or psychotic disorder

exclusion.criterion: Current alcohol or substance use disorder
exclusion.plain: Check for an active alcohol or substance use disorder

exclusion.criterion: Active suicidal ideation
exclusion.plain: Screen for current suicidal ideation

exclusion.criterion: Current psychotherapy primarily focused on CBT (other psychotherapy is allowed)
exclusion.plain: If in therapy, find out whether it is mainly CBT; only CBT-focused therapy excludes

exclusion.criterion: Severe depression and/or anxiety warranting a higher level of care and/or immediate psychiatric referral, per initial evaluation and study doctor's judgment
exclusion.plain: Check for severe symptoms that need a higher level of care or urgent psychiatric referral

exclusion.criterion: Any other clinical or medical reason in the study doctor's initial screening that suggests the study is not appropriate
exclusion.plain: Study doctor's overall judgment

screening_notes: The study's own eligibility evaluation decides whether anxiety and/or depression is clinically significant (I-2).
The study evaluation must also show cognitive difficulties are no worse than mild (I-5).
Aphasia severity is assessed during the eligibility evaluation; moderate or worse aphasia excludes (E-1).
Consent capacity needs to be checked in person (I-4).
Suicidal ideation screening is required (E-5).
Ask whether any current psychotherapy is mainly CBT (E-6).
The study doctor judges whether symptoms are too severe and whether there are other clinical or medical reasons not to enroll (E-7, E-8).
Confirm by interview that the patient can use an iPhone or iPad independently and has internet at home (I-7, I-8).
Check the medication history for stable antidepressant or anxiolytic dosing over the last 8 weeks (I-6).
a46c3e28a7d2d969fb61f85349bb1fa31612174a.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
a46c3e28a7d2d969fb61f85349bb1fa31612174a.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
a46c3e28a7d2d969fb61f85349bb1fa31612174a.involves: Participants use the MAYA mobile CBT app at least 2 days a week, 30 minutes each day, for 8 weeks. There are weekly check-ins with study staff, in person or by Zoom. Assessments happen at baseline and week 8. All participants use the same app version, with no placebo or control group.

094f94737ad67c2a14dc07949132f8af2444220f.overview: Adults aged 18–65 with generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) whose current antidepressant therapy (ADT) is not working well enough. The trial tests whether adding oral ABBV-932, an investigational drug, to their ADT is safe and effective compared with placebo. About 315 participants will be enrolled at about 50 sites in the United States and Puerto Rico.

inclusion.criterion: Age 18 Years to 65 Years, any sex
inclusion.plain: Confirm age is between 18 and 65

inclusion.criterion: Meets DSM-5-TR criteria for GAD, confirmed by MINI
inclusion.plain: Check for a GAD diagnosis; the MINI interview is done at screening

inclusion.criterion: Currently on protocol-specified ADT for GAD at adequate dose (per label) and duration (>= 8 weeks) with inadequate response
inclusion.plain: Check current antidepressant, that the dose is per label, that they have taken it for at least 8 weeks, and that it is on the protocol list

inclusion.criterion: Inadequate response verified by baseline HAM-A total >= 20 and CGI-S GAD >= 4
inclusion.plain: Scored at baseline: needs HAM-A >= 20 and CGI-S >= 4

exclusion.criterion: MADRS score >= 20
exclusion.plain: Excluded if MADRS is 20 or higher at screening

exclusion.criterion: New diagnosis or exacerbation of major depression in the last 6 months
exclusion.plain: Check the chart for a new major depression diagnosis or a flare in the past 6 months

screening_notes: The MINI structured interview is needed to confirm GAD.
Baseline HAM-A (>= 20) and CGI-S GAD (>= 4) are rated by a clinician.
MADRS must be < 20, so screen for depressive symptoms.
The list of allowed antidepressants is in the protocol and is not given here; confirm the patient's ADT with the study team.
Check the dose and duration (>= 8 weeks) of current ADT using medication history or pharmacy records.
094f94737ad67c2a14dc07949132f8af2444220f.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
094f94737ad67c2a14dc07949132f8af2444220f.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
094f94737ad67c2a14dc07949132f8af2444220f.involves: Oral ABBV-932 or placebo capsules (1 in 3 chance of placebo) added to current ADT for 6 weeks, then 4 weeks of follow-up. Regular visits at a hospital or clinic with medical assessments, blood tests, side-effect checks and questionnaires. Treatment burden may be higher than standard care.

37408c6208c04b4e44e6018c00835ce89bc311c9.overview: This is an open trial of a 6-module, time-variable version of Emotion Regulation Therapy (ERT), delivered by telehealth to adults in New York State with elevated worry, rumination, or self-criticism. It looks at how ERT mechanisms (attention, metacognitive, and motivation regulation, plus valued living) change over time, how well therapist and client views line up, and early signs of efficacy for distress, quality of life, and functioning.

inclusion.criterion: Age 18 to 65 years (any sex)
inclusion.plain: Confirm DOB: age 18–65

inclusion.criterion: Fluent in English (able to provide consent)
inclusion.plain: Confirm English fluency sufficient for consent

inclusion.criterion: Currently living in New York State
inclusion.plain: Confirm current NY State residence

inclusion.criterion: Access to at least one device with internet and video-conferencing capabilities
inclusion.plain: Confirm the patient has an internet device with video capability

inclusion.criterion: High self-reported worry, rumination, and/or self-criticism
inclusion.plain: Patient reports elevated worry, rumination, or self-criticism (pre-screen)

inclusion.criterion: Meets DSM-5 criteria for at least one current psychological disorder
inclusion.plain: Check for at least one current DSM-5 diagnosis

exclusion.criterion: Active suicidal ideation or intent
exclusion.plain: Check the current suicide risk assessment

exclusion.criterion: Substance dependence disorder, schizophrenia, or bipolar-I disorder
exclusion.plain: Check the problem list for these diagnoses

exclusion.criterion: Primary DSM-5 diagnosis of borderline or narcissistic personality disorder
exclusion.plain: Check whether BPD or NPD is the primary diagnosis

exclusion.criterion: Currently in therapy or receiving any type of psychosocial treatment
exclusion.plain: Confirm no current therapy or psychosocial treatment

exclusion.criterion: Psychotropic medication not stabilized for a period of at least 3 months
exclusion.plain: Check that any psychotropic has been stable for at least 3 months

exclusion.criterion: Current student at Teachers College, Columbia University
exclusion.plain: Confirm the patient is not a current TC student

screening_notes: The study team runs an online pre-screening questionnaire to assess self-reported worry, rumination, and self-criticism (I-5).
A structured clinical interview over Zoom Healthcare confirms the DSM-5 diagnosis (I-6) and screens out exclusionary diagnoses (E-2, E-3).
Suicide risk assessment for active ideation or intent (E-1).
Interview about current therapy or psychosocial treatment and the medication stability timeline (E-4, E-5).
The participant must enroll as a patient at the Dean Hope Center for Educational and Psychological Services (DHCEPS), Teachers College.
37408c6208c04b4e44e6018c00835ce89bc311c9.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
37408c6208c04b4e44e6018c00835ce89bc311c9.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
37408c6208c04b4e44e6018c00835ce89bc311c9.involves: Open-label telehealth ERT (6 modules) with no placebo: 12-22 weekly sessions, plus 18-28 weekly online Qualtrics questionnaires (2 before, 12-22 during, and 4 after treatment).

d980423af2980f738dcc05a625788fb03780c816.overview: The study is recruiting 100 adults: 50 diagnosed with OCD and 50 healthy controls. It combines computational modeling with EEG to look at how interacting neurocognitive subcomponents drive compulsivity, going beyond the habit vs. goal-directed model. The aim is to inform more personalized OCD treatment.

inclusion.criterion: Age 18-55 years (registry age limit 18 Years to 55 Years; all sexes)
inclusion.plain: Confirm DOB places patient between 18 and 55

inclusion.criterion: English-speaking
inclusion.plain: Confirm patient speaks English

inclusion.criterion: Right-handed
inclusion.plain: Confirm handedness is right

inclusion.criterion: Able to provide consent
inclusion.plain: Confirm capacity to give informed consent

exclusion.criterion: OCD group: meets diagnostic criteria for certain other psychiatric disorders (not specified)
exclusion.plain: Note comorbid diagnoses; ask study team which ones exclude

exclusion.criterion: OCD group: taking psychiatric medication or had behavioral treatment for OCD within a certain timeframe (not specified)
exclusion.plain: Check current psych meds and recent OCD therapy (e.g., ERP/CBT)

exclusion.criterion: OCD group: unsafe to participate in research
exclusion.plain: Check for safety concerns (e.g., acute risk); study team decides

exclusion.criterion: Healthy controls: any current psychiatric disorder
exclusion.plain: Confirm no active psychiatric diagnosis

exclusion.criterion: Healthy controls: lifetime history of certain psychiatric disorders (not specified)
exclusion.plain: Review past psychiatric history

exclusion.criterion: Healthy controls: taking psychiatric medication now or in the past
exclusion.plain: Confirm no current or past psych medication

exclusion.criterion: Healthy controls: parent or sibling diagnosed with OCD
exclusion.plain: Check family history for OCD in first-degree relatives (parent/sibling)

exclusion.criterion: Healthy controls: unsafe to participate in research
exclusion.plain: Check for safety concerns; study team decides

screening_notes: Several exclusions are left vague in the record: which comorbid disorders, which lifetime disorders, how far back the medication/therapy window goes, and what counts as 'unsafe'. The study team needs to define these.
The study team will need to confirm the OCD diagnosis and screen for comorbidities, likely with a structured diagnostic interview (method not stated in the record).
For the OCD group, ask about current psychiatric medication and recent behavioral treatment (washout or timeframe not stated).
Healthy controls need lifetime psychiatric and medication history, plus first-degree family history of OCD.
Handedness and English ability can be checked by self-report or interview.
d980423af2980f738dcc05a625788fb03780c816.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
d980423af2980f738dcc05a625788fb03780c816.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
d980423af2980f738dcc05a625788fb03780c816.involves: Cognitive tasks analyzed with computational modeling, plus EEG recording; no treatment or placebo described. Number of visits and duration are not stated.

80c4e01912d758973839247481e3c570d848f51f.overview: This trial is for children aged 7 to 15 of any sex whose parent reports in writing that the child has depression or depressive symptoms. It looks at how music therapy, recitals, and reflecting on performance anxiety and sharing creativity affect depression and resilience.

inclusion.criterion: Age 7 Years to 15 Years; all sexes
inclusion.plain: Check that the child is 7 to 15 years old. Any sex can join.

inclusion.criterion: Must indicate depression -or symptoms thereof by parent in writing
inclusion.plain: Get the parent's written statement that the child has depression or depressive symptoms.

inclusion.criterion: Children only in Amend II
inclusion.plain: Check that the participant is a child. This part of the study does not enroll adults.

screening_notes: The record lists no exclusion criteria ('none').
Eligibility depends on the parent's written report of depression or symptoms. The record does not require a formal diagnosis or a minimum score.
The CDI (depression) and Connor-Davidson (resilience) scales are listed as study measures, not entry cutoffs.
The record says 'half will be followed by recitals' but does not say whether this means half of the sessions or half of the children. Ask the study team.
80c4e01912d758973839247481e3c570d848f51f.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
80c4e01912d758973839247481e3c570d848f51f.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
80c4e01912d758973839247481e3c570d848f51f.involves: 11 weekly one-hour music therapy sessions. Half are followed by recitals at the Third Street Music School Settlement, where the children observe, interact, and discuss how performing feels. Depression (CDI) and resilience (Connor-Davidson) are measured. No placebo is mentioned.

c8b955be97a876e5ecc76d57dbfa465987fbbf95.overview: This is a randomized proof-of-concept study at the New York Presbyterian Burn Unit. It compares virtual reality (VR) plus standard opioid care against standard care alone for pain during procedures such as dressing changes and physical therapy. It wants awake, ambulatory burn patients with small burns (under 15% TBSA) who don't need conscious sedation.

inclusion.criterion: Age 8 years and older (Sex: ALL; no maximum age)
inclusion.plain: Confirm age ≥8; any sex

inclusion.criterion: Burn injury, currently in the Burn Unit at New York Presbyterian
inclusion.plain: Confirm burn diagnosis and NYP Burn Unit admission

inclusion.criterion: Awake, alert, ambulatory
inclusion.plain: Check mental status and mobility notes

inclusion.criterion: Burn comprises less than 15% total body surface area (TBSA)
inclusion.plain: Check documented TBSA <15%

inclusion.criterion: Does not require conscious sedation (e.g., ketamine) for staple removal or wound dressing changes
inclusion.plain: Check procedure/sedation orders for no ketamine or conscious sedation

inclusion.criterion: Able to give informed consent
inclusion.plain: Confirm capacity to consent

exclusion.criterion: Cognitive disorder, psychotic disorder, or bipolar I diagnosis (by self-report of previous diagnosis)
exclusion.plain: Ask patient about prior cognitive, psychotic, or bipolar I diagnosis; review chart

exclusion.criterion: Current opioid abuse
exclusion.plain: Check for active opioid misuse in history or tox notes

screening_notes: The record contradicts itself on age: the summary says 50 adult patients, but eligibility says 8 years and older. Ask the study team whether minors are enrolled. If they are, find out how consent and assent work, since I-6 requires the patient to consent.
E-1 is decided by self-report of a previous diagnosis, so the patient must be interviewed.
E-2 (current opioid abuse) needs a clinical screen. The record doesn't define it or name a test.
For I-3 and I-5, check the patient's current status and sedation needs on the day of the procedure.
c8b955be97a876e5ecc76d57dbfa465987fbbf95.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
c8b955be97a876e5ecc76d57dbfa465987fbbf95.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
c8b955be97a876e5ecc76d57dbfa465987fbbf95.involves: Randomized to VR during painful procedures plus standard opioid care, or standard care alone (no VR). No placebo. Number of visits and length of participation are not stated.

2536bf5a0dd66b780558f8d0fbfdac16ad596776.overview: This trial tests whether an adapted version of the WHO's Self-Help Plus (SH+) stress management program helps international students at The New School. It wants students aged 18 or older with at least mild distress (PHQ-4 ≥3). It measures perceived stress, anxiety, depressive symptoms, social support, self-efficacy and cultural adjustment.

inclusion.criterion: Enrolled as an international student at The New School
inclusion.plain: Confirm international student enrollment at The New School

inclusion.criterion: Age 18 years or older (no upper limit)
inclusion.plain: Check DOB: ≥18 years

inclusion.criterion: Willing to provide informed consent and complete study assessments
inclusion.plain: Confirm willingness to consent and complete 3 surveys

inclusion.criterion: Score of ≥3 on the PHQ-4, indicating at least mild distress
inclusion.plain: Give PHQ-4 and confirm total ≥3

inclusion.criterion: Sufficient English proficiency to comprehend intervention materials
inclusion.plain: Check English is good enough to follow workshop materials

exclusion.criterion: Severe psychiatric conditions requiring immediate intervention (e.g., active psychosis, severe mood disorders)
exclusion.plain: Rule out active psychosis, severe mood disorder or other acute psychiatric need

exclusion.criterion: Visual, hearing, or neurocognitive impairments that prevent engagement with the intervention
exclusion.plain: Check for sensory or cognitive impairment that would block participation

exclusion.criterion: Advanced degree in psychology or mental health-related fields (prior knowledge bias)
exclusion.plain: Ask about any advanced degree in psychology or mental health

exclusion.criterion: Score of 2 or higher on PHQ-4 Item 3 or Item 4 (frequent thoughts of self-harm or severe distress)
exclusion.plain: Exclude if PHQ-4 Item 3 or Item 4 is ≥2

screening_notes: Give the PHQ-4 at screening. The total must be ≥3 to qualify (I-4), but a score of ≥2 on Item 3 or Item 4 excludes (E-4). Both rules apply together.

Mismatch in the record: it describes Items 3 and 4 as self-harm or severe distress. On the standard PHQ-4, these are the depression items (little interest or pleasure; feeling down, depressed or hopeless), and the PHQ-4 has no self-harm item. Ask the study team which version and items they mean.
A clinical interview is needed to rule out severe psychiatric conditions needing immediate care (E-1).
Check English proficiency and any sensory or neurocognitive limits by interview (I-5, E-2).
Ask the student directly about their education history (E-3).
2536bf5a0dd66b780558f8d0fbfdac16ad596776.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
2536bf5a0dd66b780558f8d0fbfdac16ad596776.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
2536bf5a0dd66b780558f8d0fbfdac16ad596776.involves: Adapted WHO SH+ program: a two-day in-person group workshop (animated videos, interactive activities, group discussions), plus 3 surveys (before, right after and 6 weeks later) and an optional feedback interview. The record does not mention a placebo or control group.

c8dee3a760a714f636c4b0c85502d33dd36fb673.overview: The study wants adults (≥18) with advanced cancer who are on active oncologic treatment and have clinically significant anxiety (HADS-A ≥8 for at least 1 month). It compares two music-based treatments for anxiety. It also looks at whether they improve social connection and change how people cope, and whether those changes are linked to lower anxiety.

inclusion.criterion: Age ≥ 18 years (no upper limit); any sex
inclusion.plain: Confirm DOB shows age ≥18

inclusion.criterion: Pathologically confirmed advanced cancer: stage III/IV lung; any-stage pancreatic; unresectable cholangiocarcinoma, liver, or ampullary/peri-ampullary; other stage IV GI; stage III/IV ovarian/fallopian tube; other stage IV gyn; stage IV breast; stage III testicular; any stage IV GU; stage IV sarcoma, melanoma, or endocrine; lymphoma, myeloma, or leukemia
inclusion.plain: Check the pathology report and staging/resectability against the qualifying list

inclusion.criterion: Currently receiving oncological treatment
inclusion.plain: Confirm active cancer treatment in the oncology notes

inclusion.criterion: English or Spanish-speaking
inclusion.plain: Confirm preferred language

inclusion.criterion: Ambulatory, Karnofsky performance score of 60 or higher
inclusion.plain: Check the documented KPS is ≥60

inclusion.criterion: HADS anxiety subscale score of 8 or higher
inclusion.plain: Give or review HADS-A; needs ≥8

inclusion.criterion: Anxiety symptoms lasting at least 1 month
inclusion.plain: Confirm anxiety has lasted ≥1 month

inclusion.criterion: Greater than 6-month expected survival per treating oncologist
inclusion.plain: Get the oncologist's estimate that survival is >6 months

inclusion.criterion: Initiation or change in PRN anxiety medications allowed within past 4 weeks and during study
inclusion.plain: PRN anxiolytic changes are allowed and do not exclude

inclusion.criterion: Access to an internet-connected device
inclusion.plain: Confirm patient has an internet-connected device

inclusion.criterion: Able to provide informed consent
inclusion.plain: Confirm capacity to consent

inclusion.criterion: Willing to adhere to randomization, session attendance, and assessments
inclusion.plain: Confirm willingness to be randomized and attend sessions

exclusion.criterion: Diagnosis of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or substance abuse
exclusion.plain: Check the problem list and psychiatric history for these diagnoses

exclusion.criterion: Score of 10 or higher on Blessed Orientation-Memory-Concentration indicative of dementia
exclusion.plain: Give BOMC; record wording is unclear, see screening notes

exclusion.criterion: Receipt of music therapy within the past six months
exclusion.plain: Ask about music therapy in the past 6 months

exclusion.criterion: Currently receiving any form of psychotherapy
exclusion.plain: Confirm no current psychotherapy

exclusion.criterion: Initiation or change in scheduled anxiety medications (e.g., anxiolytics, sedatives, hypnotics, antidepressants) within the past 4 weeks
exclusion.plain: Review the medication list for scheduled anxiety medicines started or changed in the last 4 weeks

exclusion.criterion: Plan to initiate or change scheduled anxiety medications during the study
exclusion.plain: Confirm no planned changes to scheduled anxiety medicines

screening_notes: HADS anxiety subscale (≥8) must be given or confirmed at screening
BOMC: the record lists 'Score of 10 or higher ... indicative of dementia' as a criterion without saying include or exclude. It probably means a score ≥10 excludes, but confirm with the study team
Expected survival >6 months requires the treating oncologist's judgment
Karnofsky performance score ≥60 needs to be documented
Medication review: no scheduled anxiety medicine changes in past 4 weeks or planned during study; PRN changes allowed
Interview needed for anxiety lasting ≥1 month, music therapy in past 6 months, current psychotherapy, device access, and willingness to be randomized
c8dee3a760a714f636c4b0c85502d33dd36fb673.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
c8dee3a760a714f636c4b0c85502d33dd36fb673.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
c8dee3a760a714f636c4b0c85502d33dd36fb673.involves: Randomized to either AI-assisted songwriting with a music therapist or music listening and discussions with research staff about music culture and history; no placebo (both arms active); number of visits and duration not stated.

a471c86055f8e678c8fec9329d4b53051c9291cd.overview: This trial wants adult Veterans (age 18 or older, any sex) whose primary diagnosis is OCD. Half the sample will be OCD only and half will have both OCD and PTSD. It is a 4-year multisite randomized trial with 160 participants. It tests whether ERP delivered by VA video telehealth (VTH) improves functioning, quality of life, and OCD symptoms compared with a stress management control, both overall and in the OCD+PTSD group.

inclusion.criterion: Age 18 Years to no max; Sex: ALL
inclusion.plain: Confirm age is 18 or older; any sex can enroll.

inclusion.criterion: Veteran with primary diagnosis of OCD (50% of sample) or comorbid OCD and PTSD (50% of sample)
inclusion.plain: Confirm Veteran status, OCD as the primary diagnosis, and whether PTSD is also present.

inclusion.criterion: Receiving care at MEDVAMC (Houston, TX), Ralph H. Johnson VAMC (Charleston, SC), or VISN 20, VISN 2, or VISN 6 Clinical Resource Hub
inclusion.plain: Confirm the patient gets care at one of these sites (VISN 20: WA/OR/AK; VISN 2: NJ/NY/northern PA; VISN 6: NC/VA).

inclusion.criterion: Willingness to participate in Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP)
inclusion.plain: Ask whether the patient is willing to do ERP.

exclusion.criterion: Significant cognitive impairment
exclusion.plain: Check the chart for significant cognitive impairment.

exclusion.criterion: Conditions that threaten safety: current psychosis, mania, imminent suicidality including plan or intent
exclusion.plain: Rule out current psychosis or mania, and suicidality with a plan or intent.

exclusion.criterion: Treatment-interfering moderate to severe substance use
exclusion.plain: Check for moderate to severe substance use that would interfere with treatment.

exclusion.criterion: Taking psychotropic medications but not on a stable dose for at least 6 weeks prior to enrollment
exclusion.plain: Check that any psychotropic dose has not changed for at least 6 weeks before enrollment.

screening_notes: The study requires OCD as the primary diagnosis and records PTSD status because enrollment is split 50/50 between OCD only and OCD+PTSD. The record does not name the diagnostic method; a structured diagnostic interview is likely, so confirm with the study team.
Willingness to do ERP has to be asked directly in an interview.
Cognitive impairment, psychosis, mania, and suicide risk (plan or intent) need a clinical screen.
Substance use needs a severity assessment to decide whether it is moderate to severe and would interfere with treatment.
Review the medication history to confirm any psychotropic dose has been stable for at least 6 weeks.
a471c86055f8e678c8fec9329d4b53051c9291cd.compensation: Not stated in the registry record; ask the study team.
a471c86055f8e678c8fec9329d4b53051c9291cd.benefits: None stated in the registry record.
a471c86055f8e678c8fec9329d4b53051c9291cd.involves: Randomized to 16 weekly VTH ERP sessions or 16 weekly VTH stress management sessions (control, no placebo). Assessments happen after treatment and 6 months later; the ERP group also completes a satisfaction survey and a qualitative exit interview.

c6340dc607762bcec36c3bbd46bdc1cc3787bd02.overview: This study looks at how stress, anxiety, and negative affect change learning and decision-making, specifically reward adaptation and emotion prediction errors. It has two groups. Aims 1-3 enroll healthy adults with no neurologic or psychiatric history. Aim 4 enrolls adults with generalized anxiety disorder (GAD).

inclusion.criterion: Age 18-65 years (both groups; all sexes)
inclusion.plain: Confirm DOB: 18 to 65 years

inclusion.criterion: Speaks, reads, and writes English fluently (both groups)
inclusion.plain: Confirm fluent English

inclusion.criterion: Willing and able to follow study procedures and give informed consent (both groups)
inclusion.plain: Confirm capacity to consent and willingness to take part

inclusion.criterion: Aim 4 only: diagnosis of GAD
inclusion.plain: Check chart for a documented GAD diagnosis

exclusion.criterion: Aims 1-3 only: history of, or medication for, neurologic or psychiatric disease
exclusion.plain: Healthy-volunteer group: no neuro/psych diagnoses and no psychotropic meds

exclusion.criterion: High blood pressure or heart condition (both groups)
exclusion.plain: Check problem list for HTN or cardiac disease

exclusion.criterion: Diabetes, food allergies, metabolic disorders, or history of eating disorder (both groups)
exclusion.plain: Check for diabetes, food allergies, metabolic disorders, or any past eating disorder

exclusion.criterion: Use of corticosteroids or beta-blockers (both groups)
exclusion.plain: Check med list for steroids or beta-blockers

exclusion.criterion: Pregnancy (both groups)
exclusion.plain: Confirm not pregnant

exclusion.criterion: Aim 4: lifetime bipolar disorder or any psychotic disorder
exclusion.plain: Check for any history of bipolar or psychotic disorder

exclusion.criterion: Aim 4: substance use disorder in past 3 months
exclusion.plain: Check for SUD within the last 3 months

exclusion.criterion: Aim 4: eating disorder in past 6 months
exclusion.plain: Check for an eating disorder within the last 6 months

exclusion.criterion: Aim 4: current major depressive disorder (past MDD is allowed)
exclusion.plain: Rule out current MDD; past episodes are OK

ITI-1284 is given alone or added to other medicines. It enrolls two groups: roll-over participants who finished lead-in study ITI-1284-301 or ITI-1284-302, and de-novo participants who are new to the program and diagnosed by SCID-5-CT.

The trial compares three 6-week, self-directed online skills trainings for coping with distress: attention skills, attention plus reflective thought skills, and health and wellness education.
